Sign-preserving Q16.16 exponentiation matches the web node's bipolar behavior: sign(signal) × abs(signal)^exponent. Fixed-point log2 plus interpolated 2^x gives bounded per-sample work and avoids repeated fractional roots; output saturates. Since 914, exponent one returns the input exactly without logarithm/table evaluation; exponent zero retains the existing sign output.

drift.webBehavior: Uses double-precision sign-preserving power for all finite signal and exponent values.
drift.firmwareBehavior: Uses saturating Q16.16 log2 and interpolated 2^x with sign-preserving output. Exponent one is exact and bypasses the approximation from 914.
drift.requiredWork: Measure target CPU margin and numerical error across representative audio-rate exponent modulation.

Live durations 0–60 seconds, minimum attack 45 samples. The firmware measures a trigger-only gate length after decay; the web engine measures it from the trigger edge. 915 uses an exact quotient/remainder ramp for unchanged durations, refreshing immediately after time modulation or elapsed-position changes; ADSR timing and existing drift are unchanged.

drift.webBehavior: Provides an end trigger output when the envelope finishes and measures trigger-only gate length from the trigger edge, including delay, attack, and decay.
drift.firmwareBehavior: Renders the envelope signal but does not implement end trigger output; it begins a trigger-only gate-length hold after decay reaches sustain.
drift.requiredWork: Implement and validate the envelope completion operation in firmware and lowering, and align trigger-only gate-length timing with the web engine, then remove the blocked output rule.

911 reads package versions 1–4; the compiler emits version 4 with an ordered six-control Params descriptor list. Opcode 52 is MIDI Note. Opcodes 29–31 require 905, 32–37 require 906, 38–40 require 907, 41 (bend scaling) requires 908, 42–43 (feedback read/write) require 909, and 44–51 require 910. Older firmware rejects unfamiliar opcodes before replacing a preset.
256 operations/registers, 128 values, 32 state entries; capacity is not a measured CPU budget.

Pitch, sustained load and new-node late-buffer performance require measurement; memory fit is insufficient. A user report of increasing late buffers with test-fm-3 motivated the 914 neutral-operation fast paths. Offline host comparisons do not establish target deadline compliance; device render time and late-buffer growth must be checked after installation. 915 lifts constant/Params-only calculations out of the sample loop and caches them until values change; desktop regression/performance checks do not prove hardware deadline compliance.

FM dialog inventories enabled nodes recursively through enabled groups, using this register to show unsupported, partial and unknown support with node locations. Advisory node warnings can include unused nodes; compiler errors gate upload. Feedback loops compile when all other support and resource rules pass. Target firmware is the register version, not a detected device version. No DSP or firmware behavior changes.

Since 913, bend instructions clamp the exponent to -32 through 32 and the ratio to 12000 before the following bounded multiplication, matching the compiled WASM operation order. Each bend is applied separately in saved link order. Q16.16 ratios use nearest rounding and an interpolated Q2.30 table; tiny ratios can round to zero. Does not add MIDI pitch-wheel input. Hardware audio and timing unverified. 914 returns the exact unity ratio immediately for a zero exponent.

drift.webBehavior: Compiled links apply each bend separately: clamp the exponent to -32 through 32, compute double-precision 2^x, clamp the ratio to 12000, then multiply and clamp the result to ±12000. Opposing bends need not cancel after intermediate clipping.
drift.firmwareBehavior: 913 matches those instruction boundaries and limits using Q16.16 ratios with table interpolation. Ratios below half a Q16.16 step round to zero; multiplication truncates to fixed-point precision.
drift.requiredWork: Wider fractional precision is needed for extreme negative bends and very small products. Measure hardware timing and audible results; no runtime verification is claimed.

features.notes: Graph cycles lower to paired feedback read/write instructions sharing one state slot. The state is cleared when a patch loads or switches. Q16.16 history differs from the browser's floating-point history; hardware behavior is unverified.

drift.webBehavior: Graph cycles use a stored floating-point value, read before the cycle and written after it on every sample.
drift.firmwareBehavior: Paired package instructions read and write a reset-on-load Q16.16 history value with the same one-sample ordering.
drift.requiredWork: Measure hardware timing and audible stability under representative feedback gains.

features.notes: Shared compiler order: weighted sources, average set links (or local base), add, multiply, then individual bends. Since 913, value loads, divide-by-one copies, add/subtract/multiply/divide and bend ratios use the compiled WASM ±12000 graph bounds at every instruction. Applies to ordinary links and generated link-strength stages. Existing package versions and opcode numbers are unchanged; older firmware still accepts patches but uses the older bounds. Knob interpolation is unchanged. Host regressions verify the tested arithmetic and 915 scheduling; hardware timing remains unverified. 914 adds exact fast paths for multiplication by zero/unity, neutral bend and division by ±1/±2; no knob interpolation or feedback scheduling changes. 915 prepares control-only link and strength calculations at buffer boundaries while retaining sample-rate modulation and feedback ordering.

drift.webBehavior: Graph arithmetic uses double precision, clamps value loads and basic arithmetic to ±12000 and smooths editable values. Same-type links execute in saved order; intermediate clipping can prevent cancellation.
drift.firmwareBehavior: 913 uses the same link instruction order and graph bounds, with Q16.16 quantization and existing unsmoothed knob updates. General DSP node algorithms retain their separately registered limitations.
drift.requiredWork: Assess remaining fixed-point error and small-value underflow in host and hardware comparisons. Knob interpolation remains a separate parity gap.

features.notes: Single-assignment programs split into dependency-ordered control and audio instruction lists on load. Pure calculations depending only on values are prepared after inputs are copied at each 128-frame half-buffer boundary and reused until values change. Stateful DSP, audio-derived arithmetic, feedback and all MIDI outputs remain per sample. Packages reassigning registers retain original-order execution; legacy level smoothing uses the sample-compatible entry point. Exact envelope quotient/remainder progression avoids repeated fractional division without changing samples. No package-format, opcode, resource-limit or knob-interpolation change. Host tests establish equivalence for their fixtures, not hardware performance.

FM-1 export simplifies the lowered Q16.16 instruction stream: immutable value folding, bounded arithmetic identities, duplicate pure calculations and unused pure operations. Mutable Params values remain live, intermediate clipping is retained, and stateful/feedback execution order is preserved. Constant folding uses integer arithmetic with firmware rounding, not browser floating-point evaluation. Register numbering and asset/control value indices stay stable. This is a compiler change for firmware 915; no new firmware or package protocol. Hardware timing has not been measured.

evidenceLog.scope: Basic playback, three knobs and MIDI (transport unspecified); same-image update. Does not verify later firmware.
Two patch uploads and selection acknowledged; user confirmed playback/switching and no late buffers. Does not verify 904 DSP additions.
Installation from 903 and reboot identity only. New-node host tests statically compiled, not executed; audio and performance unverified.

ASan/UBSan host execution compared prepared rendering with original-order execution for test-fm-3 and 22 exported firmware examples, 700 buffers each, with control changes and one-sample MIDI triggers: exact output/register/state equality. A separate binary compiled from the 914 runtime produced bit-identical stereo PCM for the same 23 patches after the envelope optimisation. Cached envelope progression was checked against direct division including duration changes, repeated positions and retriggers. No hardware deadline or audio verification.

23 regression patches rendered before/after compiler optimization for 700 blocks of 128 frames with knob changes and MIDI events. ASan/UBSan renderer verifies exact stereo PCM, DSP state, feedback and delay contents. Arithmetic guards cover rounding, intermediate clipping, independent mutable controls, stateful ordering and full value pools. Feedback bend reduces from 72 to 30 instructions; no hardware performance claim.
